claims.text: KCBD reported that first responders in West Texas and the Panhandle have 24/7 access to 57 AI-powered cameras through the Xcel Energy and Pano AI partnership.
claims.quote: First responders in West Texas and the Panhandle now have 24/7 access to 57 AI-powered cameras, thanks to an ongoing partnership between Xcel Energy and Pano AI.

claims.text: Xcel and Pano AI teamed up after Xcel accepted responsibility for the Smokehouse Creek fire, the largest wildfire in state history.
claims.quote: The pair teamed up last year after the energy company accepted responsibility for the largest wildfire in state history, the Smokehouse Creek fire.

claims.text: There are 57 stations with two cameras each, set on communication towers with a 360-degree view covering about 10 miles in each direction.
claims.quote: There are currently 57 stations across the Panhandle, with two cameras per station. They’re placed on top of communication towers with a 24-hour live feed and a 360-degree view, each overlooking about 10 miles in each direction.

claims.text: When the AI cameras detect a fire, a human verifies it and narrows down the location.
claims.quote: When a fire is detected by these artificial intelligence cameras, a human will then verify it, then narrow down the location.

claims.text: Wes Reeves of Xcel said triangulating with more than one camera gives exact coordinates of a fire.
claims.quote: “There’s a map that shows, in many cases, if we can triangulate with more than one camera, we’re going to be able to see exact coordinates of those fires,” Reeves says.

claims.text: Pano AI contacts 911 to dispatch first responders and firefighters.
claims.quote: Pano AI then contacts 911 to dispatch first responders and firefighters.

claims.text: Reeves said cameras near towns pixelate any built-up environment in view.
claims.quote: “There are some that are located closer to our towns, and so if they get a camera view that’s looking over a town, it actually pixilates any kind of built-up environment.”

claims.text: Not every alert first responders get is an emergency, and Reeves said many alerts turn out to be nothing.
claims.quote: While this system is more reliable, not every alert that first responders get is an emergency. “I always remind them a lot of the alerts you might get will turn out to be nothing, but I think most people are okay with that, because they want to know everything that’s going on, especially during the high-risk times of the year.”

claims.text: Xcel paid for the camera stations upfront and will ask the PUCT to recover the costs at its next rate proceeding.
claims.quote: When these camera stations were installed, the cost was paid upfront by Xcel. This means your energy bill will not be affected yet. At its next rate proceeding, Xcel will ask the PUCT for recovery of costs.

claims.text: As of November 2025, Xcel planned 68 additional AI cameras across Texas, funded under the $490 million Texas System Resiliency Plan proposed to the PUC in December of 2024.
claims.quote: Xcel plans to add 68 additional AI cameras across Texas next year, funded under the state’s first-ever $490 million Texas System Resiliency Plan. It was first proposed to the Public Utility Commission of Texas in December of 2024.

claims.text: Xcel's December 2024 release announced more than 50 camera stations, with Carson, Gray, Roberts, Hutchinson, Wheeler, Hemphill, Garza, Cochran, Moore, Potter and Yoakum counties under consideration.
claims.quote: We are partnering with Pano AI to install more than 50 camera stations across the region. Carson, Gray, Roberts, Hutchinson, Wheeler, Hemphill, Garza, Cochran, Moore, Potter and Yoakum counties are currently being considered.

claims.text: Each Texas camera station performs a 360-degree sweep every minute.
claims.quote: Each Texas camera station will perform a 360-degree sweep every minute.

claims.text: Pano verifies a detection through human analysts, triangulates it, notifies the 911 call center, and fire departments get the live streams.
claims.quote: When a potential fire is detected, Pano immediately verifies it through human analysts, triangulates the location and notifies the 911 call center to activate the closest fire department. Fire departments will have access to these live streams for critical, real-time intelligence.

claims.text: The Smokehouse Creek fire was sparked February 26th, 2024 in Hutchinson County near Stinnett.
claims.quote: The blaze, sparked Feb. 26 in Hutchinson County near Stinnett, quickly became the largest wildfire in state history and among the largest in U.S. history.

claims.text: The Texas A&M Forest Service called the Smokehouse Creek Fire in Hutchinson County the largest wildfire in Texas history.
claims.quote: The largest wildfire in Texas history is actively burning today. The Smokehouse Creek Fire in Hutchinson County is burning a total of 1,075,000 acres across Texas and Oklahoma and is 3% contained.

claims.text: The Texas A&M Forest Service's final update put the Smokehouse Creek fire at roughly 1,058,482 acres, 100% contained, after burning more than 1 million acres.
claims.quote: The Texas A&M Forest Service announced the final update on the Smokehouse Creek fire Saturday night, saying the roughly 1,058,482-acre inferno was 100% contained.

claims.text: Xcel said on March 7th, 2024 that its facilities appeared to have been involved in igniting the Smokehouse Creek fire.
claims.quote: Minnesota-based utility provider Xcel Energy said in a March 7 statement that its facilities appeared to have been involved in igniting the Smokehouse Creek fire.

claims.text: Reeves said the cameras are about protection and getting responders to fires more quickly.
claims.quote: “It’s about protection,” Reeves says. “Obviously, we want to protect our assets, but it’s also a way to give our responders a heads up and help them do their job more efficiently and get to those fires more quickly.”

claims.text: Arvind Satyam, co-founder of Pano AI, said the technology gives responding agencies a head start and reduces the spread of fires.
claims.quote: “This is one of those areas where bringing in technology like this gives responding agencies the ability to get a head start,” Satyam says. “The advantage of that is you’re able to reduce the spread of these incidents, you’re able to protect communities, you’re also able to ensure that you’re able to manage the power grid.”

claims.text: Adrian J. Rodriguez of Xcel said the investment aims to reduce the risk of future wildfire loss.
claims.quote: “We want to better safeguard our neighbors and reduce the risk of future wildfire loss by investing in advanced wildfire detection capabilities,” said Adrian J. Rodriguez, president, Xcel Energy – New Mexico, Texas.

claims.text: Pano AI's system combines 360-degree high-definition cameras, AI-driven smoke detection and satellite data to scan continuously for smoke.
claims.quote: Pano AI’s system combines 360-degree high-definition cameras, AI-driven smoke detection and satellite data integration to continuously scan for smoke.
